messages.subject: boxplots and scales="free"
parts:
Dear list,

I´m trying to make a plot with sets of vertical boxplots. The range
of values in each set is different, so I need to use the scales="free"
argument, but I cannot make it work.

Here is a reproducible example.

# Create test data set
set.seed(100)
my.data=data.frame(code1=rep(c("A","B","C"),each=30),
code2=rep(rep(c("D","E","F"),each=10),3),
n=runif(90))
my.data$n[my.data$code2=="D"]=my.data$n[my.data$code2=="D"]*100

# Make plot
p <- ggplot(my.data, aes(x=code1,y=n)) + geom_boxplot() + coord_flip()
+ facet_grid(.~code2, scales="free")
p

What I would like to get is to have each boxplot with its own scale,
in this case between 0 and 100 for the first plot and between 0 and 1
for the other two.
Any help will be welcomed!

Julian

messages.subject: Re: boxplots and scales="free"
parts:
Hi Julian,
It works with facet_wrap (sort of -- see below). So if you only need
to facet in one dimension, you can use

p <- ggplot(my.data, aes(x=code1,y=n)) + coord_flip() + geom_boxplot()
+ facet_wrap(~code2, ncol=3, scales="free")

I really think

ggplot(my.data, aes(x=code1,y=n)) + coord_flip() + geom_boxplot() +
facet_wrap(~code2, ncol=3, scales="free_y")

should work, and it almost does, but the x-axis labels are wrong. I
think this should be viewed as a bug, and if I don't hear otherwise by
I'll file a report.

Best,
Ista
